branch_provenance.syndrome: Chronic Progressive Skin Laxity Syndrome with Yellowish Papules and Elastic Fiber Calcification

state.case_summary:
A Chinese woman in her late 20s presented with a 20-year history of progressive skin laxity. In early childhood, she had developed asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules confined to flexural areas. Subsequently, severe skin sagging occurred on her abdomen with loss of elasticity, then spread extensively with developmental growth. The patient had no extracutaneous involvement and was born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents. Her younger sister had developed the same skin symptoms.

Thick and leathery skinfolds on the neck, axillae, inguinal regions, abdomen, and limbs, with yellowish papules scattered on the dorsal neck.

- Laboratory tests:     - Low clotting activity of factor X (52.2%; reference range, 77%-131%)    - Prolonged prothrombin time (12.8 seconds; reference range, 10.4-12.6 seconds)    - Other laboratory investigations were unremarkable      - Imaging studies:    - Echocardiographic examination results were normal    - Fundoscopic examination results were normal  - Histopathology:    Image Title: Skin biopsy specimen from neck    Image Description: Shows excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments scattered in the reticular dermis (von Kossa staining)  - Genetic Testing:    Whole-exome sequencing revealed compound heterozygous sequence variation in GGCX gene:    - c.1167_1172delCTGGACinsGGGAA (p. Asn389Lys fs*13) in exon 8     - c.824C>T (p. Ser275Leu) in exon 7
